Persist Behaviors

Persist Behaviors provide the output-stage responsible for writing committed FeatureCell state to browser-accessible or external storage systems such as localStorage, sessionStorage, or custom persistence targets. Persist behaviors observe the finalized pipeline output and perform durable side effects without influencing pipeline execution.

The Persist stage operates after all upstream processing—including resolve, merge, operators, filters, and reducers—has completed. It receives the authoritative, reduced state value and is responsible solely for persistence and hydration concerns.

Persist behaviors do not transform values, do not emit snapshots, and do not participate in pipeline control flow. Their role is limited to reading and writing finalized state in a predictable, fail-safe manner.

Asynchronous Execution

Persist behaviors may execute asynchronously. When asynchronous persistence is used, the pipeline awaits completion to preserve execution order and prevent overlapping runs. Synchronous persist behaviors execute inline without affecting pipeline scheduling.

Note

Persist behaviors may be freely composed and stacked within a FeatureCell. When multiple persist behaviors are configured, each behavior is invoked in sequence during the Persist stage and receives the same final pipeline value.

Persist behaviors do not coordinate with one another and do not influence pipeline control flow. The only practical consideration when stacking persist behaviors is execution cost: persistence speed is bounded by the user’s device performance and, when custom asynchronous persist behaviors are introduced, by external I/O latency. The pipeline preserves strict execution order and does not allow overlapping runs.

Persist Stage

The Persist Stage is the final state-output stage of the Output layer. It receives the fully reduced, committed FeatureCell state and performs side-effecting persistence operations such as writing to long-term or medium-term storage. Persist behaviors never modify pipeline data and never affect whether a state update succeeds or fails.

Persist behaviors are invoked only when explicitly configured for a FeatureCell. They execute after state has been finalized and committed, ensuring that persistence always reflects the authoritative pipeline outcome. During application startup, persist behaviors may also participate in state hydration by loading previously stored values.

All persist behaviors follow a strict fail-safe model. Errors during storage access, serialization, or deserialization are caught and logged without throwing. Persistence failures never interrupt pipeline execution, block state updates, or prevent FeatureCell initialization. When persisted data cannot be loaded, the pipeline proceeds as if no stored state were present.

Persist behaviors are optional and non-destructive. When no persist configuration is supplied, the Persist stage performs no work and is effectively skipped. When present, persist behaviors provide durable state continuity across application lifecycles without introducing coupling to upstream pipeline stages.

Design Decisions

Persist behaviors expose a small, intentional surface area: writing finalized state, restoring it on startup, and clearing it when required. The table below illustrates common persistence scenarios and their expected outcomes across all built-in persist behaviors.

Persist behaviors are deliberately defensive. Serialization failures, storage quota errors, permission issues, and malformed data never throw or interrupt pipeline execution. When a failure occurs, the behavior logs diagnostic output (when enabled) and returns undefined, allowing FeatureCells to recover gracefully.

Persisted storage is cleared only as a result of an explicit state-clearing action. When a FeatureCell’s pipeline state is intentionally cleared—either by emitting a merge update with {{ `{ value: null }` }} (with clearing enabled) or by invoking vault.reset()—all configured persist behaviors remove their associated stored entries. This ensures that cleared pipeline state and persisted state remain consistent.

In contrast, destroying a FeatureCell or allowing it to be garbage-collected does not clear persisted storage. Persisted data is designed to outlive in-memory pipeline instances and remain available for future initialization. This allows FeatureCells to be torn down and recreated without losing previously persisted state, unless an explicit clear or reset operation is performed.
